findings.statement: The 40 tool handlers are listed in all-tools.ts:57-98 and the count is confirmed by reading the file.
dispatchToolCall is private, returns the MCP SDK CallToolResult type, and throws McpError for a bad argument list from outside its try block.
index.ts:126 runs main() at module scope, so a separate CLI entry is required.
loadConfig turns every bare argv token into an allowed root candidate, so tool arguments must never reach it.
No registry reaps running ffmpeg children. process-runner kills only on its own timeout.
Measured startup: 0.21 s to import the whole tool graph against a 0.02 s node baseline, with sharp at 0.19 s.
zod resolves to 4.6.5 and z.toJSONSchema exists, so describe needs no new dependency.
findings.evidence: measured by running node in mcp server/

findings.statement: Unknown argument keys are stripped silently by the dispatch parse, verified by running z.object().safeParse.
The preview is returned as base64 inside an image content block, which is wrong for a terminal.
dist is staged whole into the bundle, so dist/cli.js ships with no new staging rule.
A plugin root variable resolves inline in skill Markdown body but is absent from the Bash tool environment.
A plugin bin/ folder is on the Bash tool PATH, and a plugin with a top-level bin/ is not installed on other surfaces.
Two relative-path reads constrain the dist layout: the package.json lookup and the bundled font path.
All seven declared mirror pairs are byte-identical today, verified with cmp -s.
A skill-only reference must not enter RESOURCE_MAP or ALWAYS, because the differential compares the resource list.
choose_route can gain a cli branch without any route_contract.py schema change, because route is not a ROUTE_FIELDS member.
allocateOutputFolder always creates a new numbered folder and cannot target an existing one.
The kernel already stated that several files from one call go into one numbered folder, and the run still split the batch, so a text-only fix repeats a rule that already failed.
The only hard wait covers one name and no folder, and it is reachable only through the ambiguity escalation.
Field descriptions present an omitted fileName and subfolder as normal outcomes.
No server guard can distinguish a confirmed name from an invented one, so a guard is not worth its friction.
